findings.title: Revalidate the current logical host before returning the status used to discharge a configuration intent
findings.trigger: Complete host.configure on A, start the reconciliation host.status request to A, then switch native discovery to B with a different host_instance_id and data_dir while that status request is in flight. Release A's valid status response. A second variant switches discovery inside credentialFor for the status request, before its HTTP POST.
findings.observed: All three independent actual-DOM counterexamples show saved revision 1 with discovery already on empty-config host B. Component variants unlock the inputs and clear the pending intent. The unmodified final compiled React app accepts onConfigured and removes the first-use configuration form. B receives no requests; only A receives one host.configure. Each last status reply is returned while discovery names B, but its local_host_origin still names A and equals the original configure receipt.
findings.cause: host.status records local_host_origin once from started.discovery before credential acquisition. The post-credential identity check applies only to writes; after transport finishes callV2 returns the old origin without checking current discovery. Renderer comparison therefore compares three A snapshots, not the current host. Unlike v3's old-terminal/new-status mismatch, this is an old-status/current-host mismatch occurring inside the newly required reconciliation itself.
findings.impact: The explicit host-switch barrier can be bypassed during reconciliation: the UI discards the original-host intent and installs A's model reference into the current workbench while shell discovery points at B. B need not contain any matching configuration. This defeats the candidate's core host-origin completion guarantee.
findings.requested_change: Keep response origin and current selection validity distinct in the trusted shell. Before returning an authoritative host.status completion, re-read native discovery after asynchronous credential/transport work and reject or mark stale when logical host/data-root differ. Preserve the renderer's terminal original-host intent on this refusal and allow rechecking after return to A. Do not relabel A's response with B's origin; unchanged logical host with a new port/PID should remain eligible. Add the delayed-status and credential-yield switch cases to regression coverage.

verified_repairs: The v3 old configure-terminal/new-host-status counterexample is repaired for all six independently rerun variants: before/after terminal handoff, COMPLETED/STALE_RESPONSE and matching/different model reference. B stays locked; returning to original A with a different PID reconciles without a second configure.

The v2 in-flight component-remount race remains repaired. Whitespace correction, acknowledged remount replay, project A-to-B-to-A and unprovable terminal results pass the five independently rerun baseline DOM scenarios.

Origin is generated from trusted native discovery, not remote host_instance_id. Renderer payload local_host_origin injection is locally refused with zero HTTP; remote top-level injection is validator-refused and cannot override the local origin.
Changing only data_dir or only host_instance_id prevents replay and retains the original origin and barrier. Same logical host on a different URL/PID replays the identical original envelope.
NOT_SENT remains a pre-HTTP fact; prior ACK/possiblySent is not downgraded by later preflight or credential failures. Session writer/CAS scope and all-null first-use scope remain covered.
